parts.latex:
The life span of batteries from a particular factory is normally distributed with a mean of 840 hours and a standard deviation of 80 hours.

It is known from statistical tables that for this distribution approximately $60\%$ of the batteries have a life span of less than 860 hours.

What is the approximate percentage of batteries with a life span between 820 and 920 hours?

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{271_q37_s1}

Since $60\%$ have a life span below 860 hours and $50\%$ are below the mean of 840:

$10\%$ have a life span between 840 and 860.

By symmetry, $10\%$ have a life span between 820 and 840.

The interval 760 to 920 is within 1 standard deviation of the mean, so $68\%$ lie in it.

Hence $34\%$ have a life span between 840 and 920.

Therefore the percentage between 820 and 920 hours is
$$10\% + 34\% = 44\%$$
criteria: Recognises that $34\%$ have a life span between 840 and 920 AND attempts to use the information given regarding the statistical tables
Recognises that $68\%$ have a life span between 760 and 920, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Source wrote 'between 760 and 920' for the 68% interval (mean ± 1 SD is 760 to 920), consistent. Solution has a figure \exfigure{271_q37_s1} already in place.

271_q37_s1.notes: The normal curve is a true Gaussian (rule 10), drawn at 0.9pt and smooth with 90 samples. It is fitted to the crop's peak and shoulders, and lifted 5 px so the tails float just above the axis as in the crop. The crop's hand-drawn tails are heavier than a normal curve; this is the remaining red in the overlay. Dashed guides at 760, 820, 860 and 920 end exactly on the curve (rule 12). The 840 line is solid. Short solid ticks run below the axis to the labels, in the crop's two rows, each label clear of the lines (rule 11). The crop's axis letter z is kept.

4513.stem:
The Intelligence Quotient (IQ) scores for adults in City $A$ are normally distributed with a mean of 108 and a standard deviation of 10.

The IQ scores for adults in City $B$ are normally distributed with a mean of 112 and a standard deviation of 16.

parts.latex:
Yin is an adult who lives in City $A$ and has an IQ score of 128.

What percentage of the adults in this city have an IQ score higher than Yin's?

There are 1 000 000 adults living in City $B$.

Calculate the number of adults in City $B$ that would be expected to have an IQ score lower than Yin's.

Simon, an adult who lives in City $A$, moves to City $B$. The $z$-score corresponding to his IQ score in City $A$ is the same as the $z$-score corresponding to his IQ score in City $B$.

By first forming an equation, calculate Simon's IQ score. Give your answer correct to one decimal place.

solutions.latex:
$$\dfrac{128-108}{10} = 2$$
So $128$ is 2 standard deviations above the mean.

About $95\%$ of scores lie within 2 standard deviations, so $5\%$ lie outside, split equally between the two tails.
$$\therefore\ \dfrac{5\%}{2} = 2.5\% \text{ have an IQ score higher than Yin's}$$
criteria: Demonstrates that $97.5\%$ relates to 2 standard deviations above the mean, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Mean of City $B$ is $112$, so one standard deviation above the mean is
$$112+16 = 128$$
So Yin's score is 1 standard deviation above the mean in City $B$.

The percentage with a lower score is
$$50\%+\dfrac{1}{2}\times 68\% = 84\%$$
The expected number of adults is
$$1\,000\,000\times 0.84 = 840\,000$$
criteria: Demonstrates Yin is 1 standard deviation above the mean in City $B$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Let $x$ be Simon's IQ score. Using $z=\dfrac{x-\mu}{\sigma}$:
$$\begin{aligned} z_A &= \dfrac{x-108}{10} \\ z_B &= \dfrac{x-112}{16} \end{aligned}$$
The $z$-scores are equal:
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{x-108}{10} &= \dfrac{x-112}{16} \\ 16(x-108) &= 10(x-112) \\ 16x-1728 &= 10x-1120 \\ 6x &= 608 \\ x &\approx 101.3 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Simon's IQ score is } 101.3$$
criteria: Provides correct equation linking City $A$ with City $B$
Provides correct expression for the $z$-score for City $A$ or City $B$, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
The weight of boxes of cereal that are produced in a factory are normally distributed with a mean of 650 grams and a standard deviation of 5 grams.

Boxes of cereal are fit for sale if they weigh more than 640 grams.

If the factory produces one million boxes, how many would you expect to be fit for sale?

solutions.latex:
Find the $z$-score of $640$ g.
$$\begin{aligned} z &= \dfrac{640 - 650}{5} \\ &= -2 \end{aligned}$$
Using the normal distribution regions ($13.5\%$, $34\%$, $50\%$), the proportion above $640$ g is $97.5\%$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Number fit for sale} &= 97.5\% \times 1\,000\,000 \\ &= 975\,000 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ 975\,000 \text{ boxes}$$
